Container.Name: CADCraft
Container.Overview:
CADCraft, 2D drafting and DXF/DWG drawings in the spirit of AutoCAD, on a Selkies web desktop. It runs in your browser without a VNC client or a local install, on amd64 and arm64.
What you get: • The real Linux build of CADCraft, streamed as video by Selkies, so drawing and zooming stay smooth. • The official release package from github.com/storytold/cadcraft, checked against its published SHA-256 sum. • Settings, recent files and workspaces persist under /config.
Notes: • Open the WebUI over HTTPS on port 3001 and accept the self-signed certificate once. The Selkies client needs a secure connection; port 3000 (HTTP) is meant for a reverse proxy that terminates TLS. • Your files live under /storage (default /mnt/user, all shares), which is where CADCraft's open and save dialogs should point. • Leave WebUI Username and Password empty to run without a login, or set both for HTTP basic auth. Set them whenever the container is reachable from outside your LAN. • The app renders in software through Mesa, which is fine for documents and slower for large images and video. A passed-through Nvidia GPU takes over the video encoding of the stream (NVENC), but not the app's own drawing. • CADCraft ships new versions often; they reach this image with its next release.
Source on GitHub: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/artcraft-apps

Config.Name: WebUI Port (HTTPS / Selkies)
Config.Description: HTTPS port of the Selkies WebUI with a self-signed certificate. This is the one to open in the browser; accept the certificate once.

Config.Name: WebUI Port (HTTP / Selkies)
Config.Description: HTTP port of the Selkies WebUI, for a reverse proxy that terminates TLS in front of the container. Opened directly in a browser it shows a 'requires a secure connection (HTTPS)' error.

Config.Name: AppData (/config)
Config.Description: Persistent CADCraft settings, workspaces, recent files and logs.

Config.Name: Files (/storage)
Config.Description: The folder CADCraft opens and saves under /storage. The default /mnt/user gives access to all shares; point it at a single share to narrow that down.

Config.Name: WebUI Username
Config.Description: Optional. Username for HTTP basic auth on the WebUI. Leave it empty together with the password for no login.

Config.Name: WebUI Password
Config.Description: Optional. Password for HTTP basic auth on the WebUI. Set it whenever the container is reachable from outside your LAN.

Config.Name: Timezone (TZ)
Config.Description: Container timezone, used for log timestamps and file times.

Config.Name: User ID (PUID)
Config.Description: User ID CADCraft runs as. Default 99 (nobody on Unraid).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Permission mask for new files. The default 000 lets every container user read and write them, which suits shares that other containers touch too. Set 022 or 077 for stricter permissions.

Config.Name: Dashboard Link
Config.Description: The address you open CADCraft at in your browser, for example https://192.168.1.10:3001/. Dashboards that read container labels link to it.

Config.Name: Dashboard Group
Config.Description: The section dashboards that read container labels list CADCraft under.

Config.Name: Dashboard Name
Config.Description: The name dashboards that read container labels show.

Config.Name: Dashboard Icon
Config.Description: The logo dashboards that read container labels show.

Config.Name: Dashboard Description
Config.Default: 2D drafting with DXF and DWG in the browser
Config.Description: The short line dashboards that read container labels show under the name.

Container.Config: 2D drafting with DXF and DWG in the browser

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Name
Config.Description: The same name under the glance.* keys, which other dashboards read.

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Icon
Config.Description: The same logo under the glance.* keys.

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Description
Config.Default: 2D drafting with DXF and DWG in the browser
Config.Description: The same short line under the glance.* keys.

Container.Config: 2D drafting with DXF and DWG in the browser
